title: Application of direct current electric fields to cells and tissues in vitro and modulating wound electric field in vivo
protocol: For cells requiring CO₂-independent medium, use this type of medium for electrotaxis experiments up to 5 hours without changing the medium.
If an experiment exceeds 5 hours, exchange the medium in the system no later than 5 hours after starting.
Warm up fresh medium before exchanging old medium in the system.
For special cell types requiring specific culture media, add 10-25 mM HEPES buffer to the final medium immediately prior to the experiment.
Test appropriate concentration of HEPES for each type of cells before conducting experiments.
Inoculate stock cultures for direct adaptation at normal seeding densities and incubate in a humidified 37°C incubator with closed cap and 0% CO₂.
Monitor growth daily during direct adaptation.
Subculture cells at 80 – 90% confluency during direct adaptation.
Switch to sequential adaptation method if cell cultures fail to maintain acceptable growth over 3-5 passages.
Inoculate cells into a 50:50 (v/v) ratio of CO₂ independent medium and currently utilized medium for sequential adaptation.
Subculture flasks at 80 – 90% confluency using a 75:25 (v/v) ratio of CO₂-independent medium to the currently used medium.
Continue subculturing with 100% CO₂-independent medium.
Prepare 22 x 11 mm cover glass strips by cutting 22 x 22 mm cover glasses in half with a diamond pen.
Glue four pieces of cover glass together with 3140 silicon to form a glass well as shown in Fig. 1a, b.
Align two cover glasses parallel to each other and perpendicular to the other two.
Ensure the interior dimensions of the glass well are 22 x 10 mm for standard use.
For larger sample collection purposes, glue two pieces of 50 x 11 mm cover glass with two pieces of 22 x 11 mm ones at both ends.
Ensure the interior dimension of this glass well is 50 x 10 mm.
Allow the glass wells to dry completely overnight.
Sterilize the glass wells by autoclaving before use.
Seal the glass wells tightly to avoid leakage during cell subculture.
Maintain the four pieces of cover glass free-standing and intact during the drying period.
Use pre-cast mouldings to support the glass wells during drying if necessary.
Ensure the width of the glass well is no less than 10 mm to prevent medium leakage.
Sterilize the cover glass strips in an autoclave.
Dry the sterilized cover glass strips fully in a 60 degree oven before use.
Drill circular holes of 35 mm diameter in the center of 100 mm Petri-dishes.
Autoclave a 48 x 64 mm cover glass and dry it completely in a 60 degree oven.
Glue the sterilized cover glass with DC4 in the center of the dish to cover the hole.
Sterilize prepared dishes under ultra-violet (UV) light overnight.
Glue sterilized cover glass strips to Petri-dishes (100mm) with DC4, ensuring they line up parallel with a 10 mm gap between them.
Build four strips of 3140 silicon rubber blockers at each side of the cover glass strips, leaving a 10 mm gap at each end of the electrotactic chamber.
Ensure 3140 silicon runs to the edge of the Petri-dish side wall for watertight sealing.
Allow minimum 24 hours for 3140 silicon to solidify completely.
Load the sterilized glass well on top of the electrotactic chamber in the dish prepared in section 4(A) or 4(B).
Ensure the glass well matches the exact position of the electrotactic chamber on the dish.
Traypsinize cells to be studied.
Subculture cells into the glass well above the electrotactic chamber.
If using CO2-independent medium for EF experiments, decide whether direct or sequential adaptation is required for the cells to be studied.
Decide the density of the cells to be subcultured into the electrotactic chambers.
Transfer the chambers to a 37 degree incubator with 5% CO2 supply.
Wait 4 – 12 hours for cells to attach to the surface of the chamber.
Wash the glass well gently with fresh medium before the experiment.
Pipette away most of the culture medium from the glass well.
Remove the glass well from the electrotactic chamber.
Clean and autoclave the glass well for reuse.
Glue a number 2 cover glass roof onto two side cover glass strips to form the electrotactic chamber.
Push down the cover slip roof to minimize the depth of the chamber formed.
Take care to avoid air bubbles entering the chamber.
Drill two holes on the Petri dish lid corresponding to the ends of the electrotactic chamber.
Cover the dish with the lid, ensuring the diameter of the holes is not much larger than the glass bridges.
Prepare the system for applying electric fields to 3D cultures.
Prepare cover glass strips or slide glass for making side walls of the electrotactic chamber.
Cut cover glass or slide glass into equal-sized strips using a diamond pen.
Autoclave and dry the cut glass completely before use.
Assemble the electrotactic chamber.
Transfer Matrigel to 4°C the day before the experiment.
Pre-cool pipette tips on ice.
Pre-cool the dish or chamber on ice.
Prepare samples of tissue or organ on ice.
Transfer prepared samples to the electrotactic chamber.
Pipette out 100-200 μl Matrigel to cover the samples in the chamber.
Mix fibrinogen, aprotinin, and culture medium before preparing samples if using fibrinogen method.
Add thrombin immediately before immobilizing samples into the chamber.
Evaluate which method is most suitable for the tissue block to be investigated.
Cut 10 cm lengths of glass tubes with a diamond pen or glass saw.
Fire polish both ends of the glass tubes in a Bunsen flame to round-off sharp edges and allow maximum contact with the electrotactic chamber.
Heat the glass tubes in a Bunsen flame at about 4 cm away from both ends and bend the tubes to around 90 degrees to produce bridges shaped as in Fig. 2a and 2b.
Autoclave the glass bridges and dry in 60 degree oven.
Dissolve 2% agar powder into Steinberg's solution and autoclave the mixture.
Store prepared agar gel at room temperature for up to a month.
Heat up the agar gel until boiling in a microwave or on a hot-plate.
Fill autoclaved glass tubes with sterile plastic pasteur pipette when agar gel cools to around 60 degrees.
Prevent air bubbles from entering the tubes while filling them with agar gel.
Transfer dish containing cells/samples to be studied to temperature-controlled chamber of imaging system.
Switch on CO₂ when needed in temperature-controlled chamber.
Fill reservoirs at both sides of electrotactic chamber with CO₂-independent medium or special medium with HEPES.
Cover dish with pre-prepared lid with holes.
Fill two beakers with Steinberg's solution.
Connect the beakers of Steinberg's solution to medium reservoirs of electrotactic chamber using agar glass bridges through the holes on the lid.
Connect one beaker of Steinberg's solution to direct current power supply via Ag/AgCl electrode and electric cables.
Switch on and adjust the voltage across the electrotactic chamber using a voltage meter.
Start time-lapse recording on imaging system.
Check pH changes every 2 to 3 hours if longer recording is required.
Change the medium at the reservoirs every 5 hours during experiment.
Prepare the cross-flow system similar to the standard chamber setup.
Glue four pieces of 9 x 11 mm strips onto the Petri dish as indicated in Fig. 2c.
Add two extra 3140 blockers at each side of the gaps in the middle of the strips.
Secure silicon tubes in place to generate a closed circulation system.
Connect silicon tubes to two timer-controlled pumps.
Attach one tube with fresh medium source and the other tube with a waste beaker.
Evaluate the cross-flow speed and volume for individual experiment plan.
Set the flow system either at constant flow or interval controlled by a timer.
Ensure the fresh medium source does not run empty during the experiment.
Sterilize all tubes and containers for fresh medium before starting the experiment.
Anesthetise experimental animals with anaesthetic of choice, typically using Hypnom and Diazepam as specified.
Under the dissecting microscope, mark corneas with shallow incisions using a trephine.
Adjust the size of the circular wound according to the investigator's purpose.
Ensure the trephine incision is made to appropriate depth to leave a visible mark after washing.
Keep the stroma intact while making the circular incision evenly across the area.
Wash the corneas with sterilized BSS artificial tear solution.
Gently scrape off the corneal epithelium within the marked circular area using ophthalmologic surgical scalpels.
Ensure equal force with the scalpel across the whole area to remove the entire thickness of the epithelium.
Avoid damaging the stroma underneath during scraping.
Test and visualize the circular wound using fluorescent dye staining.
Apply three drops of aminophylline (10 mM) topically onto the wounded cornea every 2 hours for up to 36 hours.
Alternatively, apply prostaglandin E2 (0.1 mM), ascorbic acid (1 mM), or AgNO3 (1 mM) to enhance endogenous wound EFs.
Or apply ouabain (2 mM) or furosemide (1 mM) to reduce endogenous wound EFs.
Maintain the application of drugs until the wound healing process is completed.
